newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-PAKISTAN ON GUARD AGAINST BANGLADESH.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PAKISTAN ON GUARD AGAINST BANGLADESH.

text.p: Pakistan captain Rameez Raja has warned his players that Bangladesh will be tough opponents in their Asia Cup match on Wednesday.
Pakistan, who lost by 15 runs to Sri Lanka on Monday, know they must beat the ICC trophy winners at Colombo's R. Premadasa Stadium to stay in contention for the cup.
"Bangladesh is not an easy match," Rameez told Reuters.
"They (Bangladesh) have come here to play one-day cricket and I am expecting a fight from them.
"As I have said on so many occasions, the team that plays well on a particular day wins. If we focus on what we are to do, we can do it. We want to win this cup desperately."
Pakistan are not expected to make any major changes to the side which lost to Sri Lanka.
Bangladesh captain Akram Khan said his team were well prepared but looking to the future.
"We performed well in all departments to win the ICC Trophy in Malaysia early this year but we are up against superior opposition here," he said.
"Our approach is to play positive and good cricket and prepare a team for the next World Cup in England in 1999.
"Tournaments like the Asia Cup provide us with the opportunity to assess our strengths and weaknesses towards achieving that goal."
Bangladesh, who have received tremendous help from West Indian coach Gordon Greenidge, have made five changes to their team which won the ICC Trophy.

Pakistan (from): Rameez Raja (captain), Saeed Anwar, Aamir Sohail, Shahid Afridi, Inzamam-ul-Haq, Salim Malik, Moin Khan, Saqlain Mushtaq, Aaqib Javed, Arshad Khan, Kabir Khan, Shahid Nazir, Hasan Raza, Mohammad Hussain.

Bangladesh (from): Akram Khan (captain), Aminul Islam, Enamul Huq Moni, Minjahul Abedin, Athar Ali Khan, Islam Khan, Naimur Rahman, Khaled Mashud, Hasibul Hossain, Habibul Bashar, Shaikh Salahuddin, Zakir Hassan, Mafizur Rahman, Shahariar Hossain.
